extracted.name: California Farm Traditional Speculaas Cookies
extracted.description: Yani from Fondacion Argentino-Holandese de Solidaritad published the recipe for the spices in here, we experimented and went crazy! We love these cookies. Grandson is going off to college tomorrow with enough cookies till Christmas break. I found out that embossing the dough with a Holiday pattern roller works flawlessly when using cold dough the thickness of your smartphone, after dusting it with sweet rice flour. I also use a traditional wooden windmill cookie mold to make big cookies. The speculaas dough rolled around almond spice makes another special treat. See my other recipe in cookpad for sugar free speculaas cookies.
ingredient_lines: 8 Tsp cinnamon, 2 Tsp nutmeg, 1 Tsp each ginger, star anise,mace, black cardamon, cloves, pepper, coriander, grind to a fine powder
1 Tbs Speculaas Spices per 500 grams flour
For the speculaas rolls with Almond spice:
1 egg to bind spice with sugar
embossed beechwood rolling pin, well oiled in olive oil, or cookie form
Flour 60 cents, butter $1.20, sugar 30 to 60 cents, stevia 30 cents, shredded coconut 30 cents, milk 30 cents, spices 30 cents, eggs 80 cents, $3.80 for 18 large cookies,
instruction_lines: For cookies, Mix dry ingredients, add milk, egg, butter in tablespoon size cubes, mix till a smooth dough, shrink wrap, rest overnight in cool place. Dust cold Tile with tsp of rice flour, roll out 1/4 of cold dough the thickness of your smart phone.

Roll embossed rolling pin over dusted dough. Cut into large cookies, portrait size, 3” x 4”. Preheat oven to 400F degrees. Bake 10 minutes. Dust with flour. Press wooden form into cookies. Bake another 10 minutes till brown the color of molasses. Enjoy!

For speculaas filled rolls, Mix sugar, almond flour, lemon zest with egg yolk, add egg white till smooth paste. Cool. Make speculaas dough half inch thick, brush inside with water, roll around almond spice filling, trim, brush all around with egg, bake 40 minutes at 425F degrees. Cool and slice to serve.
